-- Declared by the ref's ContainerFrame.lua / PetActionBarFrame.lua / WorldStateFrame.lua -- (files we don't ship); the manage pass below overwrites them every run. CONTAINER_OFFSET_X = 0 CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y = 70 BATTLEFIELD_TAB_OFFSET_Y = 210 PETACTIONBAR_YPOS = 97 -- ref PetActionBarFrame.lua:3. Not a managed row (the manage pass computes only the Y); -- the custom block at the end of the pass recomputes it, for the reason recorded there. PETACTIONBAR_XPOS = 36
-- ref UIParent.lua:2 — the model panes' held-button spin rate (half a turn per second), -- read by every `Model_OnUpdate` transcription (the character window's + inspect's). ROTATIONS_PER_SECOND = .5
-- ref SecondsToTime (UIParent.lua:1004-1031) and its GlobalStrings, in the ref's own home -- file — two consumers now (the quest-timer window and the quest log's "Time Remaining:" -- row, decision 1150), so it lives here rather than being redefined per file the way -- BuffFrame.xml had to for SecondsToTimeAbbrev when it was the only caller. -- -- Departures, both named: -- - `GetText(TOKEN, nil, n)` is the ref's plural-aware GlobalString lookup, a C binding we -- don't ship. Its enUS rule is the singular token for exactly 1 and the `_P1` twin -- otherwise — the same rule already codified in `tooltip_item/render.rs` and MailFrame.xml -- — so it collapses to the local `plural()` below and the four shipped string pairs -- (GlobalStrings.lua:895-896, 2296-2297, 2693-2694, 3404-3405). -- - Lua 5.1 dialect: `math.mod`/`math.floor` for the 5.0 bare `mod`/`floor`. -- -- Everything else is verbatim, INCLUDING the two behaviours that look like bugs and are -- not: the thresholds are strict `>` (86400 s reads as hours, not "1 Day"), and `count < 2` -- stops after two units, so a 3-day quest reads "3 Days 4 Hrs" and never mentions minutes. DAYS_ABBR = DAYS_ABBR or "Day" DAYS_ABBR_P1 = DAYS_ABBR_P1 or "Days" HOURS_ABBR = HOURS_ABBR or "Hr" HOURS_ABBR_P1 = HOURS_ABBR_P1 or "Hrs" MINUTES_ABBR = MINUTES_ABBR or "Min" MINUTES_ABBR_P1 = MINUTES_ABBR_P1 or "Mins" SECONDS_ABBR = SECONDS_ABBR or "Sec" SECONDS_ABBR_P1 = SECONDS_ABBR_P1 or "Secs"
if not SecondsToTime then local function plural(singular, pluralForm, n) if n == 1 then return singular end return pluralForm end
function SecondsToTime(seconds, noSeconds) local time = "" local count = 0 local tempTime seconds = math.floor(seconds) if seconds > 86400 then tempTime = math.floor(seconds / 86400) time = tempTime .. " " .. plural(DAYS_ABBR, DAYS_ABBR_P1, tempTime) .. " " seconds = math.mod(seconds, 86400) count = count + 1 end if seconds > 3600 then tempTime = math.floor(seconds / 3600) time = time .. tempTime .. " " .. plural(HOURS_ABBR, HOURS_ABBR_P1, tempTime) .. " " seconds = math.mod(seconds, 3600) count = count + 1 end if count < 2 and seconds >= 60 then tempTime = math.floor(seconds / 60) time = time .. tempTime .. " " .. plural(MINUTES_ABBR, MINUTES_ABBR_P1, tempTime) .. " " seconds = math.mod(seconds, 60) count = count + 1 end if count < 2 and seconds > 0 and not noSeconds then time = time .. seconds .. " " .. plural(SECONDS_ABBR, SECONDS_ABBR_P1, seconds) .. " " end return time end end
-- ── The login seed for the extra action bars ────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- The four extra bars' visibility is stored SERVER-SIDE, in `PLAYER_FIELD_BYTES` byte 2, -- and the client never writes that byte itself — `SetActionBarToggles` only posts -- `CMSG_SET_ACTIONBAR_TOGGLES` and waits for the field to come back (wow-re -- `system/ui/scratch/action-bar-toggles.md` §5: the setter's every store is into its own -- stack frame, and nothing in the binary fires on a change to that byte). So the live UI -- state is the four Lua globals `MultiBars.xml` owns, and `GetActionBarToggles()` is read -- exactly ONCE, here, to seed them. Reading it again later would fight the optimistic -- value the options rows just set and lose a round trip's worth of clicks. -- -- This is the reference's own seam, arm for arm (its UIParent_OnEvent does the same two -- statements on the same event). `MultiActionBar_Update` is existence-guarded because the -- ~25 per-window harnesses that load this file load no bars; the binding itself is engine -- level and always installed. Decision 1500. function UIParent_OnEvent(event) if ( event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" ) then SHOW_MULTI_ACTIONBAR_1, SHOW_MULTI_ACTIONBAR_2, SHOW_MULTI_ACTIONBAR_3, SHOW_MULTI_ACTIONBAR_4 = GetActionBarToggles() if ( MultiActionBar_Update ) then MultiActionBar_Update() end end -- The ready-check popup's opener (decision 1549), ref UIParent.lua l.570-572. The -- event is the engine's own `0x218`, fired by the `MSG_RAID_READY_CHECK` open -- handler; the frame and `ShowReadyCheck` live in RaidFrame.xml, so this is the one -- place the two meet. Existence-guarded for `MultiActionBar_Update`'s reason: the -- per-window harnesses load this file without the raid pane. if ( event == "READY_CHECK" ) then if ( ShowReadyCheck ) then ShowReadyCheck() end end end
-- ── Everything that has to move when the bottom of the screen fills up ────────────────── -- -- One row per thing whose seat depends on which bars are raised. A row reads: -- -- baseY where it sits on the y axis with nothing in the way -- baseX / xOffset the same for the x axis, under two names: the rows that write a var -- spell it `baseX`, the rows that seat a frame spell it `xOffset`, and -- baseX wins if a row ever names both -- bottomLeft, bottomRight, bottomEither, pet, reputation, maxLevel (y axis) -- rightLeft, rightRight (x axis) -- what this row owes each raised bar, ADDED for every flag standing -- anchorTo / point / rpoint who to hang off; defaulted to UIParent BOTTOM-to-BOTTOM -- isVar the row is not a frame at all: it names a GLOBAL, and the pass writes -- the computed offset into it for other files to read -- -- The KEY is the global name — a frame to seat, or the var to write — and other windows' -- OnShow/OnHide drive the pass by it, so both the keys and the fields are a published -- shape. Written as one constructor rather than a dozen index assignments: it is a -- constant, and a constant reads better as a table than as a program that builds one. UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS = { -- Frames to seat MultiBarBottomLeft = {baseY = 17, reputation = 9, maxLevel = -5, anchorTo = "ActionButton1", point = "BOTTOMLEFT", rpoint = "TOPLEFT"}, GroupLootFrame1 = {baseY = 60, bottomEither = 42, pet = 42, reputation = 9}, TutorialFrameParent = {baseY = 55, bottomEither = 47, pet = 42, reputation = 9}, FramerateLabel = {baseY = 64, bottomEither = 42, pet = 42, reputation = 9}, CastingBarFrame = {baseY = 60, bottomEither = 40, pet = 40, reputation = 9}, ChatFrame1 = {baseY = 85, bottomLeft = 17, pet = 17, reputation = 9, maxLevel = -5, anchorTo = "UIParent", point = "BOTTOMLEFT", rpoint = "BOTTOMLEFT", xOffset = 32}, ChatFrame2 = {baseY = 85, bottomRight = 17, rightLeft = -88, rightRight = -43, reputation = 9, maxLevel = -5, anchorTo = "UIParent", point = "BOTTOMRIGHT", rpoint = "BOTTOMRIGHT", xOffset = -32}, ShapeshiftBarFrame = {baseY = 0, bottomLeft = 45, reputation = 9, maxLevel = -5, anchorTo = "MainMenuBar", point = "BOTTOMLEFT", rpoint = "TOPLEFT", xOffset = 30},
-- Globals to write CONTAINER_OFFSET_X = {baseX = 0, rightLeft = 90, rightRight = 45, isVar = "xAxis"}, CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y = {baseY = 70, bottomEither = 27, bottomRight = 0, reputation = 9, isVar = "yAxis", pet = 23}, BATTLEFIELD_TAB_OFFSET_Y = {baseY = 210, bottomRight = 40, reputation = 9, isVar = "yAxis"}, PETACTIONBAR_YPOS = {baseY = 97, bottomLeft = 43, reputation = 9, maxLevel = -5, isVar = "yAxis"}, }
-- ── Consumers of the VAR rows ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- A row with `isVar` leaves a NUMBER in a global and anchors nothing, so whoever seats -- itself from that number has to be told when the number changes — otherwise it keeps the -- seat it computed the first time and the bars grow underneath it. That is not a -- hypothetical: the open-bag stack read a file-local copy of CONTAINER_OFFSET_X/Y and sat -- at the no-bars corner forever, so a bottom multibar drew straight through the lowest bag -- window (director-caught, decision 1499). -- -- The reference closes the same loop by hard-calling `updateContainerFrameAnchors()` from -- the end of its own pass (UIParent.lua:1774). This is that call generalized: a consumer -- registers itself and the pass calls it after every recompute, so the NEXT var consumer -- does not have to edit this file to be noticed. Order of registration is the order of -- call; listeners are independent (nothing here reads what another writes). -- -- The law, stated once so it can be pointed at: **nothing outside this file may keep its -- own copy of a managed offset.** Read the global fresh at use, and if you cache a SEAT -- derived from it, register here. `bottom_hud_tests.rs` enforces both halves. UIPARENT_MANAGED_POSITION_LISTENERS = {}
function UIParent_RegisterManagedPositionListener(fn) table.insert(UIPARENT_MANAGED_POSITION_LISTENERS, fn) end
function UIParent_ManageFramePositions() -- Frames that affect offsets in y axis local yOffsetFrames = {} -- Frames that affect offsets in x axis local xOffsetFrames = {}
-- Set up flags. Departure: the bottom flags read the always-on bars' visibility, -- not the ref's SHOW_MULTI_ACTIONBAR_1/2 option globals (0270 ships no such state). local bottomLeftShown = MultiBarBottomLeft and MultiBarBottomLeft:IsShown() local bottomRightShown = MultiBarBottomRight and MultiBarBottomRight:IsShown() if ( bottomLeftShown or bottomRightShown ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "bottomEither") end if ( bottomRightShown ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "bottomRight") end if ( bottomLeftShown ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "bottomLeft") end
if ( MultiBarLeft and MultiBarLeft:IsShown() ) then table.insert(xOffsetFrames, "rightLeft") elseif ( MultiBarRight and MultiBarRight:IsShown() ) then table.insert(xOffsetFrames, "rightRight") end
if ( ( PetActionBarFrame and PetActionBarFrame:IsShown() ) or ( ShapeshiftBarFrame and ShapeshiftBarFrame:IsShown() ) ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "pet") end if ( ReputationWatchBar and MainMenuExpBar and ReputationWatchBar:IsShown() and MainMenuExpBar:IsShown() ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "reputation") end if ( MainMenuBarMaxLevelBar and MainMenuBarMaxLevelBar:IsShown() ) then table.insert(yOffsetFrames, "maxLevel") end
-- Walk the rows and settle each one against the flags now standing. Rows are -- independent — nothing here reads a var another row writes — so the arbitrary order -- `pairs` hands back is not a hazard. for index, row in pairs(UIPARENT_MANAGED_FRAME_POSITIONS) do local frame = getglobal(index) if ( frame ) then -- Start from where the row sits with nothing in its way. A zero base is a real -- base, not an absent one, which is why `or` chains do the right thing here. local xOffset = row.baseX or row.xOffset or 0 local yOffset = row.baseY or 0
-- Then add what the row owes each raised bar, keeping note of which ones it -- actually paid — two of them interact below. local paid = {} for _, flag in pairs(yOffsetFrames) do if ( row[flag] ) then yOffset = yOffset + row[flag] paid[flag] = true end end for _, flag in pairs(xOffsetFrames) do if ( row[flag] ) then xOffset = xOffset + row[flag] end end
-- The bottom-left bar and the pet/stance row do not simply stack: clearing both -- costs 23px more than the two figures added together. The reference carries the -- same correction (l.1657-1658) with no derivation, and it is a fact about the -- bars' art rather than arithmetic we can recompute. if ( paid.bottomLeft and paid.pet ) then yOffset = yOffset + 23 end
-- A row either NAMES A GLOBAL to leave the number in, or is a frame to seat. if ( row.isVar == "xAxis" ) then _G[index] = xOffset elseif ( row.isVar ) then _G[index] = yOffset else -- ClearAllPoints first: the row states the frame's WHOLE seat, so the pass -- must own it outright. `SetPoint` only replaces the same-NAMED point, so -- any other anchor the frame was authored with survives and fights this -- one — ChatFrame2 is declared in XML with both a TOPLEFT and a -- BOTTOMRIGHT onto ChatFrame1, and the row's BOTTOMRIGHT replaced only -- the second, leaving the pane stretched from ChatFrame1's top-left -- corner to the screen's bottom-right. Masked today only because -- ChatFrame2 ships hidden, which is the worst kind of latent (decision -- 1499). Every row here supplies a single complete anchor, so this is a -- no-op for the other eight and the reference's plain SetPoint is -- behaviour-identical on its own frames. frame:ClearAllPoints() frame:SetPoint(row.point or "BOTTOM", row.anchorTo or "UIParent", row.rpoint or "BOTTOM", xOffset, yOffset) end end end
-- Custom positioning the row table cannot express (ref l.1705-1738). Both rules -- belong to the pet/stance ROW — the one row two different bars share — and without -- them the pet bar lands on top of the bottom-left multibar's buttons -- (director-caught: the bar drew across a row of spells, border and all). -- -- (a) The shelf art IS the pet bar's border, and it only makes sense when the bar -- sits directly on the main bar. Raised a row it would draw across whatever is -- underneath, so the ref hides both strips (l.1707-1708) — the same move it makes -- for the stance bar's own end-caps, which is why benilla's stance bar has none -- (0270 anchors it statically at the raised position). -- (b) The pet bar is the only managed entry whose row is a VAR: the loop above writes -- the NUMBER PETACTIONBAR_YPOS (97, +43 with the bottom-left bar up) and anchors -- nothing, so the ref re-seats the frame with it here (l.1735-1736). -- -- Departure: the ref computes PETACTIONBAR_XPOS in ShowPetActionBar() and reads it -- here, which only works because its bar slides in over several frames. Ours appears -- at once, so the value is computed where it is used. Same rule -- (PetActionBarFrame.lua:170-174): the two bars share this row, so a pet bar shown -- while the stance bar is up starts 20px past the last stance button. That case is -- rare but real — a possessed or charmed unit gives a pet bar to a class that also -- has forms. local bottomLeftUp = MultiBarBottomLeft and MultiBarBottomLeft:IsShown() if ( SlidingActionBarTexture0 and SlidingActionBarTexture1 ) then if ( bottomLeftUp ) then SlidingActionBarTexture0:Hide() SlidingActionBarTexture1:Hide() else SlidingActionBarTexture0:Show() SlidingActionBarTexture1:Show() end end if ( PetActionBarFrame ) then PETACTIONBAR_XPOS = 36 local forms = GetNumShapeshiftForms and GetNumShapeshiftForms() or 0 if ( forms > 0 and ShapeshiftBarFrame and ShapeshiftBarFrame:IsShown() ) then local last = getglobal("ShapeshiftButton"..forms) local right = last and last:GetRight() if ( right ) then PETACTIONBAR_XPOS = right + 20 end end -- The ref guards this on IsShown() because a hidden bar of its is mid-slide and -- owns its own anchor; ours has no slide, so re-seating a hidden frame is a -- no-op and the guard would only add an ordering trap (OnShow fires the pass). PetActionBarFrame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "MainMenuBar", "BOTTOMLEFT", PETACTIONBAR_XPOS, PETACTIONBAR_YPOS) end
-- The under-minimap right stack (ref l.1740-1770): anchorY walks down capture bars → -- quest timer → durability → quest watch, each shown frame pushing the next one down -- by its own height. benilla ships the quest-timer, durability and quest-watch arms -- (below); the capture bars above them don't exist yet, so anchorY starts at the ref's -- initial 0. The reference never leaves DurabilityFrame on its static XML anchor -- (whose +40 hangs the side glyphs off-screen — director-caught): every pass seats it -- at -CONTAINER_OFFSET_X, minus 20 more when a showSeparate glyph -- (shield/off-weapon/ranged) extends the art to the right — then drops the quest -- tracker to the running anchorY so the two never collide at the same corner. local anchorY = 0 -- ref l.1753-1757 verbatim (decision 1150). Seated whether shown or not — the ref -- SetPoints unconditionally and only the height accrual is gated — so the frame is -- already in place the frame it appears. Nil-guarded like every row here: the -- durability-only test harness ships no quest-timer frame. if ( QuestTimerFrame ) then QuestTimerFrame:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "MinimapCluster", "BOTTOMRIGHT", -CONTAINER_OFFSET_X, anchorY) if ( QuestTimerFrame:IsShown() ) then anchorY = anchorY - QuestTimerFrame:GetHeight() end end if ( DurabilityFrame ) then local durabilityOffset = 0 if ( DurabilityShield:IsShown() or DurabilityOffWeapon:IsShown() or DurabilityRanged:IsShown() ) then durabilityOffset = 20 end DurabilityFrame:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "MinimapCluster", "BOTTOMRIGHT", -CONTAINER_OFFSET_X-durabilityOffset, anchorY) if ( DurabilityFrame:IsShown() ) then anchorY = anchorY - DurabilityFrame:GetHeight() end end -- QuestWatchFrame is last in the ref's walk (l.1770), seated at the running anchorY so -- it drops below the durability guy when he shows instead of overlapping him (both -- anchor this same MinimapCluster corner — director-caught). benilla's tracker is -- QuestWatchFrame; nil-guarded because the durability-only test harness (and -- any config without a quest log) ships no such frame. if ( QuestWatchFrame ) then QuestWatchFrame:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "MinimapCluster", "BOTTOMRIGHT", -CONTAINER_OFFSET_X, anchorY) end
-- Last: everything that seats itself from a var row this pass just rewrote. After the -- frames, so a listener may measure one (the bag stack reads GetScreenHeight and its -- own windows' heights, not another managed frame — but the ordering costs nothing and -- removes a class of question). for _, fn in ipairs(UIPARENT_MANAGED_POSITION_LISTENERS) do fn() end end
-- The published binding-label API — benilla's implementation of the behaviour ref -- UIParent.lua:1819-1878 specifies (decision 1008, which closed 0997's "abbreviates -- through KEY_ABBR" residue with the REAL mechanism: there never was a KEY_ABBR set, the -- whole abbreviation is this one function). Addons call it by name, so the contract is: -- -- * a nil name reads as the empty string; -- * "CTRL-SHIFT-2" splits at its LAST dash — up to and including that dash is the -- modifier run ("CTRL-SHIFT-"), what follows is the key ("2"). A name with no dash is -- all key; -- * the key renders through the `prefix..key` global (the KEY_* family), preferring a -- `_MAC` twin on a Mac client, and falls back to the raw key name; -- * returnAbbr — what the action bar's HotKey corners pass — shrinks ONE modifier to -- its initial, so SHIFT-2 reads "s-2" (the director's ask), and collapses TWO OR MORE -- to "·". The full form (tooltips, the Keybindings page) keeps the whole prefix. -- -- Two knowing departures from the reference, both about its code rather than its -- behaviour: its `gsub(tempName, "CAPSLOCK", "Caps")` line is dead — gsub returns a new -- string and that result is discarded, so nothing can observe it — and has no counterpart -- here; and its GetLocale()/IsMacClient() calls ride behind existence guards because this -- VM defines neither yet, with the getglobal fallback covering the gap.
-- What a single modifier shrinks to on a button corner. German calls Control "STRG" (the -- deDE swap below runs first), which is the one that needs two letters to stay legible. -- The order is fixed so the pass is deterministic, but it does not matter: no abbreviation -- occurs inside another modifier's name, so no substitution can feed the next. local MODIFIER_ABBREVIATIONS = { { "CTRL", "c" }, { "SHIFT", "s" }, { "ALT", "a" }, { "STRG", "st" }, }
function GetBindingText(name, prefix, returnAbbr) if not name then return "" end
local modifiers, key = "", name local modifierCount = 0 -- The greedy `.*` walks to the LAST dash, which is the one that divides the modifier -- run from the key; gsub's second return then counts the dashes, one per modifier — -- plus one more when the key ITSELF is a dash ("CTRL--"), which is why that binding -- abbreviates as if it had two. The reference's dash-walking loop reaches both of the -- same answers, and both are pinned by keybindings_tests. local _, lastDash = strfind(name, "^.*%-") if lastDash then modifiers = strsub(name, 1, lastDash) key = strsub(name, lastDash + 1) _, modifierCount = gsub(modifiers, "%-", "-") if GetLocale and GetLocale() == "deDE" then modifiers = gsub(modifiers, "CTRL", "STRG") end end
if returnAbbr then if modifierCount > 1 then -- Two modifiers never fit a corner: the whole label becomes the dot. return "·" end for _, abbreviation in ipairs(MODIFIER_ABBREVIATIONS) do modifiers = gsub(modifiers, abbreviation[1], abbreviation[2]) end end
prefix = prefix or "" local label if IsMacClient and IsMacClient() then label = getglobal(prefix .. key .. "_MAC") end label = label or getglobal(prefix .. key) or key return modifiers .. label end
-- ref UIParent.lua:1051-1057, transcribed 1:1 (decision 1062). The reference's own -- list joiner, and it is exactly as plain as it looks: a bare ", " between every item, -- with NO "and" before the last one and NO localization string of any kind — 1.12 has -- no LIST_DELIMITER/AND global for it to reach for, and it does not build one. (The -- richer `BuildColoredListString` right below it in the reference — the per-item -- met/unmet red — already lives in TradeSkillFrame.xml as a guarded global, 0437 phase -- 3; folding that one up here beside this is a follow-up, not this slice's churn.) -- -- Callers: the pet paper doll's diet tooltip and PetStable.lua's, both as -- `format(PET_DIET_TEMPLATE, BuildListString(GetPetFoodTypes()))`. -- -- ZERO arguments returns NIL, not "" — the ref reads `arg[1]` off an empty vararg and -- returns it unchanged. That is load-bearing: `format("%s", nil)` errors, so a caller -- that can pass nothing (a warlock minion's empty diet) must be gated by its own UI, and -- it is — the diet icon is hunter-only. Quietly returning "" here would hide that. -- -- Lua-5.0 `arg`/`arg.n` written as `select("#", ...)`/`select(i, ...)`, the 5.1-native -- spelling — TradeSkillFrame.xml's own substitution. function BuildListString(...) local n = select("#", ...); if ( n == 0 ) then return nil; end local list = select(1, ...); for i = 2, n do local item = select(i, ...); list = list..", "..item; end return list; end
-- BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(link) → true if it went in, else nil (decision 1059). -- -- Every shift-click site in this UI does the same two things before inserting: check the -- chat edit box is up, and — ours alone — check the link is not nil. That nil case is -- **benilla's, not the reference's**: our item templates resolve asynchronously -- (`CMSG_ITEM_QUERY_SINGLE`, answered a frame or many later), so a `Get…Link` getter -- legitimately answers nil for a slot whose name and quality have not landed, where the real -- client's synchronous item cache always has one. `EditBox:Insert` takes a string (the -- byte-modelled `0x77bee0`), so an unguarded nil is a script error — which is exactly the -- bug this function exists to make impossible to reintroduce at the next site. A dozen call -- sites were growing a dozen copies of the same two-line guard, and three of them shipped -- without it. -- -- The RETURN is what lets a caller fork on "did chat take it?" — a bag slot's shift-click -- posts the link when chat is open and opens the stack splitter when it is not (ref -- ContainerFrame.lua:567-577). Blizzard themselves eventually factored this exact helper out -- for this exact reason: 2.0's `ChatEdit_InsertLink(text)`, returning true/false, called from -- every one of these sites. 1.12 has no such function, so ours carries a benilla name rather -- than pretending to be reference API. function BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(link) if not link then return nil end if not ChatFrameEditBox or not ChatFrameEditBox:IsVisible() then return nil end ChatFrameEditBox:Insert(link) return true end
-- ── LowerFrameLevel / RaiseFrameLevel (ref UIParent.lua l.1890-1896), verbatim ──────── -- -- Two lines each, and the reason to have them is that they are FRAMEXML, not engine: an -- addon calling `RaiseFrameLevel(f)` is calling a function the client's own UI defines, and -- without it that is `attempt to call global` at load (BetterCharacterStats dies there). -- Our own ActionBar.xml already describes this operation in prose at three sites while -- doing it by hand; those can move onto the real name whenever that file is next opened. function LowerFrameLevel(frame) frame:SetFrameLevel(frame:GetFrameLevel() - 1) end
function RaiseFrameLevel(frame) frame:SetFrameLevel(frame:GetFrameLevel() + 1) end
-- ── The 1024x768 scale ratios (ref UIParent.lua l.1794-1802) ──────────────────────────── -- -- Two FrameXML helpers addons call by name (the raid pullouts and a dozen third-party -- drag handlers), so they exist for the reason `MouseIsOver` and `RaiseFrameLevel` do: -- missing, the caller dies on `attempt to call global`. The reference's constants are the -- 1024x768 reference resolution, and its own callers multiply a `GetCursorPosition()` -- reading by them to convert into pixel space. -- -- **benilla's own drag code does NOT use them**, and that is deliberate rather than an -- oversight: our UI space is 1:1 logical px and `GetCursorPosition` already reports in -- the same space `SetPoint` offsets are read in (the same identity `MouseIsOver`'s -- comment below records for `GetEffectiveScale`). Multiplying here would place a dragged -- frame at 1.5x the cursor on a 1600-wide window. Kept for the addons, unused by us. function GetScreenHeightScale() return GetScreenHeight() / 768 end
function GetScreenWidthScale() return GetScreenWidth() / 1024 end
-- ── MouseIsOver: is the cursor inside this frame, with optional per-edge padding ───────── -- -- The idiom every hover-driven addon writes, and **9 corpus addons call it** by name. -- Missing, each is `attempt to call global 'MouseIsOver'`. So the CONTRACT is 1.12's, quirks -- and all (ref UIParent.lua l.1388-1417) — three of which look like bugs and are not: -- -- · each offset is ADDED to its own edge, in that axis's positive direction. A positive -- `topOffset` raises the ceiling (growing the box upward) while a positive -- `bottomOffset` raises the floor (shrinking it from below). The reference's own caller -- proves the intent: `MouseIsOver(chatFrame, 45, -10, -5, 5)` is 45 up into the tab -- strip, 10 in from the bottom, 5 out each side. -- · the padding is ALL OR NOTHING on `topOffset`: pass none and the other three are -- dropped with it, so `MouseIsOver(f, nil, 5)` silently ignores the 5. Pass a topOffset -- and omit any of the rest and it is an arithmetic error, not a zero — 1.12 raises -- there too, and an addon written against it may lean on either half. -- · the bounds are strict, so a cursor exactly on an edge is outside. -- -- A frame that has never been laid out answers nil for its rect; nil is the right answer to -- hand back for it, and the reference's own comment on that guard ("a symptom not the real -- issue") is about where the unresolved frame came from, not about the guard. -- -- ONE DIVERGENCE, and it is a no-op: the reference divides the cursor by -- `frame:GetEffectiveScale()` because 1.12 hands Lua screen pixels. benilla's UI space is -- 1:1 logical px and `GetEffectiveScale` is the constant 1 (`script/pointer.rs`, -- `object.rs` l.271), so the division is written out rather than left in to divide by one -- forever. If a real UI scale ever lands, this is one of the sites that needs it back. function MouseIsOver(frame, topOffset, bottomOffset, leftOffset, rightOffset) local x, y = GetCursorPosition() local left, right = frame:GetLeft(), frame:GetRight() local top, bottom = frame:GetTop(), frame:GetBottom() if not left then return end if not topOffset then topOffset, bottomOffset, leftOffset, rightOffset = 0, 0, 0, 0 end -- All four edges are padded before any of them is tested, and deliberately so: folding -- the additions into the comparison would let a short circuit swallow the arithmetic -- error that a half-supplied offset set is supposed to raise. left, right = left + leftOffset, right + rightOffset top, bottom = top + topOffset, bottom + bottomOffset if x > left and x < right and y > bottom and y < top then return 1 end return nil end
